experiments.name: PKSmart direct molecular CL candidate
experiments.reason: The acquired target is human total IV clearance, not human hepatic clearance. It is reserved for a separate total-CL model and was not mixed into the hepatic benchmark.

diagnostic_findings: OOD is the dominant reliability problem; the current AD separates a lower-error in-domain group from a high-error OOD group but is not yet a validated accuracy-recovery route.
Observed upstream error magnitude was not a statistically reliable predictor of downstream absolute log error in this N=30 diagnostic (fu Spearman 0.197, p=0.297; HLM Clint Spearman 0.095, p=0.619).

The largest candidate errors include Warfarin, Atorvastatin, Diazepam, Sunvozertinib, Digoxin, Metformin, Verapamil, and Osimertinib; this is consistent with mixed chemical space and clearance-mechanism limitations, not a single safe global offset.
ood_analysis.gating_decision: Do not convert OOD labels into silently improved predictions; retain low-confidence/fail-closed routing until matched human hepatic/nonrenal development data support a route.

next_highest_value_action: Acquire record-level human hepatic/nonrenal clearance and human hepatocyte Clint with resolvable species, matrix, assay, fu_inc, Rb, and IV context; keep CL_TOTAL_IV in a separate development track.
